Self-assess your knowledge. Express yourself and get feedback from our instructors.

Two trains are traveling in opposite directions with speeds of 60 km/hr and 45 km/hr respectively. They take 15 seconds to cross each other. If the two trains are traveling in the same direction, then a person sitting in the faster-moving train would have overtaken the slower train in 40 seconds. Find the length of the trains (in m).

properties.html: A train can travel 25% faster than a car. They start from the same point, at the same time, and both reach their destination,200 km away from the starting point at the same time. If the train had lost 30 minutes of time in halting at different stations. Find the speed of the train (in kmph).

properties.html: A train started from station A for a journey towards station B and met with an accident at 120 km from station A. It completed the remaining journey at 5/6 of its previous speed and reached 2 hours late at station B. Had the accident taken place 300 km further, it would have been only 1 hour late. What is the usual speed of the train?

properties.html: Royal Caribbean's Wonder of the Seas (WOTS), the world's largest cruise ship, having a length of 365 m is going upstream and crosses another cruise ship MS Lona of length 90 m going downstream. If the speed of WOTS in still water is 36 km/hour, speed of MS Lona is 54 km/hour and speed of the river current is 5 m/s, then find the time taken by the two ships to cross each other such that the initial separation between their fronts is 270 m.

properties.html: A boat started from a point in a river and traveled a certain distance upstream, after which it turned back and returned to its starting point. The boat covered this round trip in 6.5 hours. The net speed of the boat upstream was 37.5% less than the net speed of the boat downstream. How much more time (in minutes) did the boat take to travel upstream than what it took to travel downstream?

properties.html: The speed of boat A in still water and the speed of stream B are 40 km/hr and 20 km/hr, respectively. The speed of boat B in still water and the speed of stream A are 'x' km/hr and 'y' km/hr, respectively. The sum of time taken by boat A to cover 450 km upstream and the same distance downstream in stream A is 24 hours and the sum of the time taken by boat B to cover 320 km upstream and 320 km downstream in stream B is 12 hours. Find (x + y).
